question: Is 308 Evergreen Street, Hillsdale, NJ the correct property address, or is this a data entry error?
why_it_matters: TCR's service area is centered on Johnson City, TN with a 45-mile radius; Hillsdale, NJ is approximately 800 miles outside that area, and the scope references TDEC (a Tennessee regulatory body), suggesting the address may be wrong.

question: Is the property at 308 Evergreen Street on a septic system or connected to city sewer?
why_it_matters: Scope explicitly requires TDEC septic coordination (scope.pdf); if the property is on septic, the 4–6 week TDEC process must start by ~2026-09-01 to protect the 2026-10-12 start date.

question: Has existing main electrical service amperage been verified to confirm the 100A subpanel can be added without a service upgrade?
why_it_matters: Scope includes a 100A subpanel (scope.pdf / breakdown CSV); per addition job-type rules, amperage verification is mandatory before contract is locked — if the main service is at capacity, a service upgrade adds cost and schedule time.

question: Has TDEC been contacted to initiate the septic inspection process, given the ~6-week window required before excavation?
why_it_matters: Scope requires TDEC coordination (scope.pdf); with a 2026-10-12 start date and TDEC typically taking 4–6 weeks from first contact to permit-in-hand, the window to initiate closes around 2026-09-01 — approximately 7 weeks from today.

question: Is the tankless water heater included in this contract, or is it excluded and the existing gas water heater vent simply being extended?
why_it_matters: Breakdown title says 'Incl. Tankless WH Option' and section is 'HVAC – Mini Split, Tankless WH & Relocations', but scope.pdf only references extending the existing gas WH vent — the discrepancy affects procurement, plumbing rough-in sequencing, and the $6,503.36 HVAC section budget.

question: Have John Simons' material selections (tile, flooring, fixtures, paint) been finalized ahead of the 2026-10-12 start?
why_it_matters: TCR policy prohibits scheduling until customer selections are locked (CLAUDE.md); master bathroom has custom tile shower finishes and the addition has full interior finishes — if selections aren't confirmed ~3 weeks before start (by ~2026-09-21), procurement cannot fire and the schedule is at risk.

question: Has the signed contract been executed and the 25% deposit received from John Simons?
why_it_matters: TCR policy requires both signed contract and 25% deposit before demo begins (CLAUDE.md); job status is 'waiting_work' with no contract confirmation recorded, and demo start is ~13 weeks out.

question: Has the 3/12-into-6/12 roof tie-in structural condition above the existing ceiling been assessed, or should a concealed-condition discovery buffer be built into the schedule?
why_it_matters: Scope describes a 3/12 pitch tying into existing 6/12 (scope.pdf), which per addition job-type rules is the most reliable change-order source on an addition — hidden rafter conditions or framing incompatibilities at the tie-in are common and expensive.

question: Is the existing heat pump relocation sub already scheduled for a pre-demo window (minimum 3 working days before main demo starts on ~2026-10-12)?
why_it_matters: Scope includes relocating the existing heat pump and electrical disconnect as part of site work (scope.pdf / breakdown CSV); per addition rules, this must happen in site_prep before demo — if the HVAC sub isn't booked, demo cannot start on schedule.

question: Does the new addition floor or roof load actually bear on the existing LVL beam location (3-ply 14", ~15'-6" span opening the load-bearing wall per scope.pdf)?
why_it_matters: If the new floor/roof load bears on the LVL location, new exterior framing cannot start until the LVL is installed; if independent, the LVL sub-chain runs in parallel — this determination changes the critical path by up to 3–4 working days.

question: Is the future elevator shaft (~4'x4' per scope.pdf) physically located inside the new addition footprint, or does it require cutting into existing structure?
why_it_matters: The shaft framing is described without explicit placement in the addition objective areas (scope.pdf); per retrofit detection rules, a new feature with no stated location is presumed retrofit — if it's inside existing structure, it must be scheduled as a separate retrofit component independent of new framing.
